steps.text: Melt peanut butter and butter together in a medium saucepan over low heat; stir often.

Mix confectioners' sugar and cereal together in a large bowl until well combined. Pour in peanut butter mixture and stir until well combined; mixture will be crumbly but will hold together when pressed.
Form into 1-inch balls; place on parchment-lined cookie sheets. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate until firm, 3 hours to overnight.
Melt chocolate in a double boiler over low heat.

Place 1 peanut butter ball into chocolate; use 2 forks to roll in mixture to coat. Let excess chocolate drip back into the pot; place on a wire rack set over parchment paper. Repeat with remaining peanut butter balls.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Butter Balls
raw_recipe.description: This peanut butter balls recipe is a no-bake wonder—rich and creamy from peanut butter, crunchy from rice cereal, and dipped in a chocolaty coating.

review.reviewBody: I've made these for years with slightly different proportions: 2 cups crunchy peanut butter, 2 cups powdered sugar, 2 cups rice krispies and 1 1/2 cups softened margarine. I, too, melt the choc. chips in the microwave with shortening. I went to a Party City and bought a plastic dipping spoon in the candy-making department....and it makes dipping the balls a MUCH easier process! Even when I double the recipe, every morsel goes.....as I place them on pretty plates or in pretty candy dishes and give them as Christmas gifts to very special friends!

Oh my does this bring back memories! My Grandma Helen used to make these every Christmas and we all looked forward to them. I didn't have her recipe and I was so happy to find this on AR. I made these with my niece and we had a ball - no pun intended! I did made a couple of changes to made it hold together better. I used a whole jar of peanut butter (it's a little over 2 cups anyway), kept the butter the same, and reduced the sugar by 1 cup. I melted the peanut butter and butter in the microwave and then mixed everything. I put the peanut butter balls on cookie sheets lined with wax paper and let them chill for a few hours. I then dipped them in chocolate and red and green sprinkles for Xmas. Take one bite of these crunchy, peanuty, chocolatey little treats and you'll want to make these every year too!

I've been making these for 40 years however used crushed graham crackers instead of rice cereal. This year - going gluten free, so using crunchy peanut butter and no filler. CROCKPOT for melting. I have a small dip crockpot and it is the easiest way to go. Did the double boiler maker for years, messy, and dangerous. Also, add a tablespoon of shortening to harden the chocolate faster and give it a pretty sheen. Favorite of all my family and friends, so make around 200 every year.

After reading other reviews I reduced the sugar to 1 1/2 cups and added an extra cup of cereal as it looked too wet. Was making for a dinner party where a guest was GF so I used roughly crushed rice chex cereal instead of rice krispies. They have such a great texture and flavor! I haven't had a lot of success trying to dip stuff in chocolate so I placed the rolled balls on a rack over a large sheet pan and poured the melted chocolate (with a touch of heavy cream) over the balls. Will definitely be making these during the holidays -and all year round!

A very good recipe, very popular with friends at parties. A couple of suggestions -- We cut the sugar down to 1.5 cups, and it tastes great. The full four cups would make these unbearably sweet. Also added about another half cup of peanut butter, to make up the lost volume. Another thing I've learned is that the peanut butter and cereal mixture is very difficult to work with until it's cooled down quite a bit. Put it in the fridge for a few minutes, and it's much easier to roll into balls. Also a question on the yield -- this says 24 servings. I get 50 to 60 one-inch peanut butter balls out of it, so that probably needs to be corrected. You'll get a lot more out of this than you expect.

Like others have said, with a full 4 cups of sugar it's simple too sweet. What I do to balance it out is use 1&½ cups powdered sugar and a of cup almond flour. I also replace a ½ cup of regular peanut butter with unsweetened peanut butter and they taste much better now! 

Also a good trick when rolling the mixture into balls; dole out some globs then roll a few at a time with greesed hands, cleaning your hands when they get sticky to help keep the balls together
Delicious! I used only 1 cup of confectioners' sugar and these were perfect. Not too sweet, just right.

This is just like the recipe that my friend & co-worker Kelly made long ago, except using only 2 cups of powdered sugar....4 is too much. The rice crispies add great texture and crunch. Some use crunchy PB, as well, but I strongly prefer using creamy for these. I make these every Christmas to give as gifts. I found it too tedious dipping each ball one at a time, so I now line mini muffin tins with the mini liners, put 1 TB of melted chocolate in the bottom of each liner, drop in the ball and cover with more melted chocolate. You can decorate with Christmas sprinkles or finely chopped peanuts on top before they harden. They look beautiful & festive, taste delicious, and are very popular with everyone who receives them. They look so cute in the mini muffin liners! :-)

I wanted to make peanut butter balls that were both gluten-free and without corn additives. I followed the recipe as written but substituted Kellogg's Gluten Free Rice Crispies and used Kraft All Natural peanut butter. The result was fantastic. I used three cups of rice crispies and three cups of icing sugar. Suggest you keep hands water-wet when rolling balls. Will definitely make again.

Yummy! Kind of like a crunchy Reese's Peanut Butter Cup. Mixture was very sticky (probably because I reduced sugar to 3 C) so I kept a water bowl nearby to rinse finger frequently. Recipe was still plenty sweet. Dipped only bottom portion of ball in the "Buckeyes" style. 
Will definitely make again.

way way way too sweet. Cut confectioners sugar in half in order to make palatable for most people. Otherwise only children maybe like it. Suggest melting chocolate compound for dipping with two forks. Freezing balls for half an hour before dipping makes them set up very quickly.
I’ve had to use 3-1/2 cups of peanut butter with additional butter to make these stick. I think either reduced the amount of icing sugar or increase the peanut butter by a cup.
Very sweet, cant even taste the peanut butter. Also way to sticky to roll into balls. I ended up making a 8x8 pan of peanut butter rice Krispy squares and just poured the melted chocolate on top.

Pretty much the same recipe I've been making for 30 years and it's always a hit. Everyone wants to know if I'm making them every Christmas. I do add a few tablespoons of melted canning wax to the melted chocolate to make the balls look shiny and not dull.

Diabetic friendly modifications : I used half regular icing sugar and half stevia icing sugar, 1 cup of chopped salted peanuts and 1 cup of crispy rice cereal and would probably use 2 and 3/4 cups of peanut butter. Was really delicious!
Way too crumbly. I ended up pressing the mix into a baking pan and made squares
I absolutely love this recipe, but recently I have wondered if adding cream cheese Would be a good idea if so, I’m wondering, how much would I have to adjust all the other ingredients?

I've never heard of pb balls with rice cereal. You don't need it. The recipe is missing vanilla extract and you should use unsalted real butter. Instead of chocolate chips ( they are bitter) use Hershey chocolate bars .

I honestly don't know how this recipe has the traction it does. It is entirely TOO SWEET! I will make another batch with half the confectioners sugar and edit this review. Honestly, you could barely taste the peanut butter. I do like the rice crispies though.
These came out perfect always think additions
